enonce_markdown: Which sentence is the passive form of "The cook prepares the meal every day"?

choix.texte: The meal is preparing by the cook every day.
The meal was prepared by the cook every day.
The meal has prepared by the cook every day.
The meal is prepared by the cook every day.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

To change an active sentence into the passive, make the object the new subject, keep the tense of the verb and use the matching form of "be" with the past participle. The doer, if kept, follows "by".

### Solution

**Answer: d.** The active verb is in the present simple, so the passive is "is prepared". "Is preparing" is not a passive, "was prepared" changes the tense to the past, and "has prepared" lacks "been" and is not passive.

enonce_markdown:
Choose the form that completes the sentence correctly.

"A new school ________ in our village next year."
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The passive of a future form is will + be + past participle.

### Solution

**Answer: b.** The school does not build itself and "next year" is future, so "will be built" is needed. "Will build" and "is building" are active, and "will been built" is not a possible form.

enonce_markdown: Which sentence is the passive form of "Someone is cleaning the hall"?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The passive of a continuous tense uses the continuous form of "be" (am/is/are/was/were being) and the past participle.

### Solution

**Answer: c.** The action is in progress now (present continuous), so the passive is "is being cleaned". "Is cleaned" is the present simple, "has been cleaned" the present perfect and "was being cleaned" the past continuous.

enonce_markdown: Which is a correct passive form of "They gave the winner a trophy"?

choix.texte: The winner was given a trophy.
The winner is given a trophy.
A trophy was given the winner.
The winner was gave a trophy.

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A verb with two objects (give someone something) has two passives. Keep the tense, use the past participle, and keep "to" if the thing becomes the subject.

### Solution

**Answer: a.** "Was given" keeps the past simple of the active sentence. "Is given" changes the tense, "A trophy was given the winner" needs "to" ("A trophy was given to the winner"), and "was gave" uses the wrong participle.

enonce_markdown:
Rewrite each sentence in the passive voice.

(a) The headmaster must sign every report card.
(b) Farmers in Ndop grow rice on the plain.
(c) The mechanic was repairing the lorry when it began to rain.
(d) Someone has stolen my bicycle.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Make the object the subject, keep the tense and the modal, and put the right form of "be" before the past participle. The agent after "by" can be dropped when it is unknown or unimportant.

### Solution

(a) Every report card **must be signed** by the headmaster.

(b) Rice **is grown** on the plain by farmers in Ndop.

(c) The lorry **was being repaired** (by the mechanic) when it began to rain.

(d) My bicycle **has been stolen**.

| Sentence | Active verb | Passive verb |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | must sign | must be signed |
| (b) | grow | is grown |
| (c) | was repairing | was being repaired |
| (d) | has stolen | has been stolen |

**Common mistakes**

1. Forgetting "be" after a modal ("must signed").
2. Changing the tense, for example "was repaired" instead of "was being repaired" for (c).
3. Keeping "by someone" in (d), where the agent is unknown.

enonce_markdown:
Rewrite each sentence as indicated, keeping the meaning.

(a) People believe that the doctor saved many lives. (Begin: The doctor ...)
(b) They expect that the minister will visit the town. (Begin: The minister ...)
(c) A tailor is sewing my uniform. (Begin: I ... and use "have" or "get".)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Reporting verbs (believe, expect, say) allow a personal passive with an infinitive (is believed to ...; for an earlier action use to have + past participle). To say that someone else does a service for you, use have/get + object + past participle.

### Solution

(a) The doctor **is believed to have saved** many lives. (The saving happened before the present belief, so the perfect infinitive is needed.)

(b) The minister **is expected to visit** the town. (The visit is in the future, so the simple infinitive is used.)

(c) I **am having my uniform sewn** (by a tailor). ("I am getting my uniform sewn" is also accepted.)

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing "is believed to save" in (a), which changes the time of the action.
2. Writing "I am sewing my uniform" in (c): the speaker does not sew it; someone else does.
